questions.question:

Let us look into the meaning of other words:

 
• 'Continued' means without a break in continuity; ongoing.
 
• 'Initiated' means cause (a process or action) to begin.
 
• 'Adopted' means legally take (another's a child) and bring it up as one's own.

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'observed' is grammatically correct because it means to notice or perceive (something) and register it as being significant.

Here, people are in wonder about the bird's flight by observing them fly. So, 'observed' is the correct word.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 2.
questions.solution:

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word.

Congested
questions.solution:

__
 
• **'Congested**' means crowded with traffic or people as to hinder or prevent freedom of movement.

 
 
• **Example** - Traffic still gets **congested **because of the bridge construction.
 
 
 
• **'Cleared'** means getting rid of objects or obstructions.
 
 
• **Example **-Someone had **carefully** cleared the area.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement

While the teacher was scrutinizing the sums, Swaminathan was __gazing on__ his face.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2.

'gazing at' is grammatically correct because 'at' is used to express location or arrival in a particular place or position.

So, 'on' is grammatically wrong because it means to be physically in contact with and supported by (a surface). 

The correct preposition that follows *gaze* is *at*. Example - *to gaze **at **the scenery.*

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Ram cannot withdraw all his money unless he does not give a prior notice.
questions.solution:
**The correct solution is option 4.**

'unless he does not give' is grammatically incorrect because 'unless' means except if.

Here, 'unless' and 'does not' are contrary to each other. So, it's wrong. 

__Correct sentence__: *Ram cannot withdraw all his money **if** he does not give prior notice.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• “if” is conditional. It is used to describe a possible situation, and what would happen under the conditions of that situation
 
 
• **For E.g.-** "**If **you don't save some money, you can't go on vacation
 
 
 
• “Unless” is also conditional, but it is effectively “if” with an extra exclusion or negative qualifier added
 
 
• **For e.g.-** You can't go on vacation **unless** you save some money.

questions.question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E bought cars which were priced differently. B's car was costlier than C's car but was less costly than E's car. A's car was costlier than D's car but less costly than C's car. Whose car was the 2nd costliest?
questions.solution:
According to the given information,

B's car was costlier than C's car but was less costly than E's car

E > B > C

A's car was costlier than D's car but less costly than C's car

E > B > C > A > D

B’s car is the second costliest.

Hence, “B” is the correct answer.

Similarly,

The place value of B is 2

The place value of O is 15

BOSS = 2 + 15 + 19 + 19 = 55

Hence, “55” is the correct answer.

questions.question: The volume of a sphere is 36π cm³. What is the radius of the sphere?

• **Majuli** is a river island in the Brahmaputra River, Assam.
 
• It is the **largest inhabited riverine island** in the world.
 
 
 
• **Krishna**: Krishna River originates at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
 
 
• The river outfalls into the **Bay of Bengal.**
 
• **Ghataprabha River, Malaprabha River, Bhima River, Tungabhadra River, and Musi River** are its major tributaries.
 
 
 
• **Ganga**: It is a trans-boundary river of Asia which flows through India and Bangladesh.
 
 
• It rises in the Himalayas in the Indian state of **Uttarakhand** and eventually empties into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, which gives every child aged 6-14 the fundamental right for education, was assented to in which year?
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 4__ i.e 2009.**

__
 
• The Right to Education Act (RTE) Act of the Parliament of India was enacted on 4 August 2009 and came into force on 1 April 2010. 
 
• This act is also known as the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act because of its provision of, *“the fundamental right of every child between the ages of 6 to 14 with specifies minimum norms in elementary schools.”*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

Important Provisions of RTE are as follows:

__
 
• Right of children to free and compulsory education till completion of elementary education in a neighbourhood school.
 
• It makes provisions for a non-admitted child to be admitted to an age-appropriate class.
 
• It specifies the duties and responsibilities of appropriate Governments, local authorities, and parents in providing free and compulsory education.
 
• It lays down the norms and standards relating to Pupil Teacher Ratios (PTRs), buildings and infrastructure, school-working days, and teacher-working hours.
 
• According to the RTE Act, a teacher will spend a minimum of 45 hours in teaching including preparation hours in a week and will be prohibited from the practice of private tuition.
 
• It provides for the appointment of appropriately trained teachers, i.e. teachers with the requisite entry and academic qualifications. 
 
• The act prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment.
 
• It provides for the development of curriculum in consonance with the values enshrined in the Constitution, and which would ensure the all-around development of the child.

Thus, the RTE-Act of 2009 provides the right of free and compulsory education to each child aged 6 to 14 years.__
